summary.headline: HMA Agro FY26 standalone revenue rose 39.2% to INR 67,689 million, with EBITDA up 80.3% to INR 2,109.5 million.
summary.overview: Management described FY26 as the company's strongest year, with standalone revenue of INR 67,689 million (up 39.2% YoY) and standalone PAT of about INR 1,271 million. Q4 FY26 standalone revenue was INR 15,384.83 million, up about 4% YoY from INR 14,368.2 million. Consolidated revenue was INR 69,164.95 million (up 34.7%) with consolidated EBITDA of INR 2,839.59 million and margin of about 4.11%. The Q&A was short and several answers were deferred to email, including geography split, Philippines target, and rice revenue.

segments.name: Standalone
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue of INR 67,689 million and EBITDA of INR 2,109.5 million; margin up to 3.12%, attributed to operating leverage, higher capacity utilisation, product mix and cost control.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue of INR 69,164.95 million and EBITDA of INR 2,839.59 million; management cited higher capacity utilisation, improved pricing and product mix.

segments.name: Rice
segments.commentary: Management said rice is a small segment with repeat orders and a growing client base; FY26 contribution was not disclosed on the call and will be shared later.

guidance_outlook: Management referred to a target of INR 10,000 crore (INR 1 billion as stated in the call) revenue in FY27 and said the team is working to reach it as early as possible; no firm timeline was given.
Management expects pricing headroom as Australia and New Zealand raise prices, but gave no quantified price guidance.
Pipeline initiatives mentioned at an early stage: frozen French fries and chicken, with no volumes or timelines disclosed.
capex_capacity: Management said a Malaysian authority approval for one of its subsidiaries' plants enabled higher utilisation of that plant; no capex amounts or commissioning dates were given.
No capacity, utilisation percentages or new capex plans were quantified on the call.
demand_pricing: Management reported stronger demand from existing customers and new international buyers across major verticals, and expansion into a new geopolitical market.
Philippines buffalo meat 25% target for FY26 was not achieved; the Philippines market buys only selected products, and the company is working to educate buyers to take a wider range.
Southeast Asian (Vietnam, Malaysia) domestic prices are higher due to limited livestock; management said pricing is currently working but gave no percentage discount to local peers.
Freight and logistics costs have risen sharply due to Middle East conflict; management warned that continued high freight could pressure product pricing.
Input buffalo prices are influenced by weather, transport cost, seasonal harvest and farmer demand; management said it cannot fully control procurement prices.

qa_highlights.question: Geographic split of FY26 revenue across top five geographies?
qa_highlights.answer: Not provided on the call; management will email a continent-wise breakdown.

qa_highlights.question: Was the 25% Philippines sales target for FY26 achieved?
qa_highlights.answer: No. The target was not achieved because the Philippines buys only selected products; the company is working on educating buyers to use a wider range.

qa_highlights.question: How do the company's buffalo meat prices compare with local peers in Vietnam, Malaysia and the Philippines?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said local domestic prices there are higher due to limited livestock and import dependence; it gave no percentage discount and will follow up by email.

qa_highlights.question: How is the Middle East situation affecting operations and what drives input cost inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Freight and shipping costs have risen many-fold and could pressure pricing if unresolved. Input costs depend on demand-supply, weather, transport and farmer pricing; the company cannot fully pass these on.

qa_highlights.question: Update on the rice business and FY26 contribution; is INR 1 billion FY27 revenue on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Rice has repeat orders and a growing client base but the FY26 figure was not disclosed. Management reiterated the INR 1 billion FY27 target and said it aims to reach it soon.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for product portfolio expansion, and the pricing basis for the OFS?
qa_highlights.answer: Early-stage plans include frozen French fries and chicken, with no numbers. The OFS floor price was set by the board on current market value to achieve minimum public shareholding via a stock exchange window; management said SEBI rules allow the seller to set the price.

risks_watch: Freight and logistics cost escalation from Middle East conflict could squeeze margins if customers cannot absorb higher prices.
Buffalo input cost volatility linked to weather, transport and farmer pricing, with limited ability to pass through costs.
Philippines market concentration risk: buyers take only selected products, and the FY26 target was missed.
Rice segment contribution undisclosed; FY27 INR 1 billion revenue target needs to be tracked against the disclosed figures.
Pending follow-ups: continent-wise geography split and price comparison vs local peers promised by email.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on headline growth and record FY26 results, but cautious on freight, geopolitics and input costs. Answers on the Philippines target, rice contribution and OFS pricing were vague or deferred to email.
key_quotes: FY2526 has been our strongest financial year in the history of company, with record performance across revenue, EBITDA, EBT, PBT -- PAT.
If this geopolitical situation does not normalized, sooner it will really give us very bad rate on our product pricing.
We are working very hard to achieve this target as soon as possible before the target deadline, what we have said.

growth.why: Management targets INR 1 billion (INR 10,000 cr per analyst framing) revenue in FY27 as early as possible with no firm timeline; Q4 FY26 standalone revenue grew about 4% YoY, and backing is limited to stronger demand, pricing headroom and high-capacity utilisation with no quantified capacity, orders or capex.
